newsitem.title: CROATIA: U.S. Navy frigate docks in historic Dubrovnik.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy frigate docks in historic Dubrovnik.

text.p: The U.S. Navy's guided-missile frigate USS Klakring docked in the historic Croatian seaside town of Dubrovnik on Tuesday, local authorities said.
It was the first U.S. warship to visit Croatia since the country won independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, according to the Italy-based U.S. Sixth Fleet.

The frigate was to remain in Dubrovnik, a beautiful walled town known as the "Pearl of the Adriatic," for three days with its crew meeting Croatian naval officers for discussions on non-combat topics.
Croatian Defence Minister Gojko Susak and Peter Galbraith, the U.S. Ambassador to Croatia, were expected in Dubrovnik on Wednesday to join the talks.
The Klakring has 25 officers, 16 chief petty officers and 183 enlisted personnel, the Sixth Fleet said.
It described the visit as a step furthering regional peace and stability in postwar former Yugoslavia.
